Scaramucci’s Bitcoin Investment Outlook
Scaramucci made the comments in a Saturday post on X, acknowledging that he is not “technically allowed to give investment recommendations.”
Despite this, he still explained his perspective. “I always say: 1-2% of your money should be in something like Bitcoin,” he wrote.
I’m not technically allowed to give investment recommendations, but…
I always say: 1-2% of your money should be in something like Bitcoin.
I’m not saying sell your house, donate a kidney, and buy Bitcoin.
That’s NOT what I’m saying.
I’m saying this is something that is…
Scaramucci cautioned against going to extremes, saying he wasn’t telling anyone to sell a house or “donate a kidney” to buy Bitcoin.
A 1%-2% weighting is a modest position size. It gives investors exposure to Bitcoin while limiting the effect of its sharp price swings on a total portfolio.
Younger Investors Are Driving Crypto Interest
Scaramucci said Bitcoin is “catching on,” pointing to his own children as an example of growing interest among younger investors.
He said they are “way more digitally competent” than he is. According to Scaramucci, they want “a little of this” in their portfolios.
“That generational instinct means something,” he wrote. “Pay attention to it.”
BTC Slips Below $60,000
According to Coinbase data, Bitcoin was trading at $59,979.75 at 8:37 p.m. EST on Saturday. The exchange’s price page showed that it had risen by $1,171.75, marking a 1.99% increase.
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July and is down more than 50% from its record near $126,000, set in October 2025.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have shed about $3.47 billion in November, including a record $541.1 million outflow from
iShares Bitcoin Trust
on Thursday.
